title: Prove universal dyadic rank-one borrowed-hub realization (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Every dyadic rank-one common-chart shear admits one borrowed source as its sole readout hub, with source-only preparation and exact restoration. This is a scoped constructive proof extending David Ganz / Dugongue's #4502 sufficient single-pivot adapters, using #4494's integer factorization setting.

```text
M = a b, b primitive integral
prepare X_0 = bX using integer source ADDs
Y_j += a_j X_0 once per nonzero target row
reverse preparation and restore every source
```

Only `research/dyadic-rankone-borrowing/` is added. The theorem permits every finite matrix size; the standalone compiler and verifier have explicit finite input limits. No extra field, clean entry, CLEAR, SCALE or odd-denominator native coefficient is required. Classical Bezout, Euclidean reduction and uncomputation retain their existing credit. Produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

- Before: #4502's sufficient source and target pivot methods both exclude its explicit `[[9,15],[15,25]]` fixture because the needed ratios are not dyadic.
- After: the new compiler realizes the fixture exactly, including arbitrary dirty inputs and restoration, with one readout hub. Complete bill: 32 ADDs, allowance 270. Direct entrywise evaluation costs four ADDs and allowance 76; lower scalar cost is not claimed.
- Exact symbolic replay passes 3,939 exhaustive two-by-two parameter cases, 768 wider fixtures, two named fixtures and three coefficient/role/Euclidean boundary cases. Nine invalid inputs reject, and five mathematical omission controls detect missing preparation/restoration/readout, a wrong hub and a wrong inverse order.
- Both registered commands pass locally with warning-strict CPython 3.12, each in about 0.77 seconds; the complete registered launcher took 1.83 seconds. These are check durations, not performance comparisons. AST parsing, function-size inspection and whitespace checks pass. No separate Python linter or type checker is installed locally.
- Official committed export integrity and read-only Git-free normal/optimized replays pass.
- Committed-byte and declared source-history preflight pass at `391355b8e537b82cedabd45af509177496e7a7a6`. Receipts are generated by the verifier and bound to all six package files.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/dyadic-rankone-borrowing/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/dyadic-rankone-borrowing/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-rankone-borrowing
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/dyadic-rankone-borrowing --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace the interpreter path. Expected mathematical marker: `PASS_DYADIC_RANKONE_BORROWING`; registered marker: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

## Limitations

The new result is universal admissibility of this one-hub topology. Direct entrywise ADDs already give a zero-scratch implementation of arbitrary dyadic shears. No circuit optimality, favorable actual native window, coefficient-growth bound, rounded precision, physical caller, stock/tape bill, supplier admission or new kappa is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed; no Lean build or selected cold replay was run.

The original card's historical ceiling example raises `KeyError: 'complex_profile'` against the changed selected schema. It was attempted, left unchanged and not used as evidence. Current selected metadata orientation passes separately. The selected frontier remains unchanged.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this common-chart rank-one borrowed-hub admissibility question was found in the publication refresh. #4502 and #4505 are merged predecessors: the former supplies sufficient pivot adapters, and the latter installs its four specific native windows. Their results are cited, not audited or replayed.

## Open next questions

1. Can a short unimodular preparation improve the complete bill on an actual no-pivot native window? First identify one such window and compare direct evaluation, both pivot methods and the full preparation/readout/restoration invoice.
2. What coefficient-growth and rounded-error bounds admit the method in a real caller? First bound all intermediate row norms for one concrete preparation and its inverse. No numerical precision prescription is supplied here.

## CI notes

## Merge danger

Two-way door; blast radius is the isolated research package. No shared code, frozen source, predecessor credit or selected-frontier file changes.
